request.description: Get unified timeline (activities + tasks when Pro is active). Use this for the 'All Activity' tab. Each item includes a 'display_status' field: 'upcoming', 'due_today', 'completed' for activities; 'upcoming', 'due_today', 'overdue', 'completed' for tasks. For upcoming-only view, use GET /activities/upcoming instead.

Get upcoming activities and tasks (today onward, sorted ascending by nearest first). Backend handles date filtering and sort order automatically. Each item includes a 'display_status' field: 'upcoming', 'due_today', or 'completed'. Also supports deal filtering via entity_type and entity_id.
Get unified timeline for a specific deal (Pro required)

request.description: Get all deals associated with a specific contact
Create a new deal linked to a contact. Required: title, contact_id, pipeline_id, stage_id
Get all tasks associated with a specific contact
Get all tasks associated with a specific deal (Pro required)
Create a task linked to a contact using contact_id
Create a task linked to a deal using deals parameter (Pro required)
Mark multiple tasks as completed in a single request. Returns the number of tasks affected and a success message. Sales reps can only complete their own tasks.
Mark multiple tasks as pending in a single request. Resets completed_at and reminder_sent_at timestamps. Sales reps can only update their own tasks.
Delete multiple tasks in a single request. Uses POST method instead of DELETE for better client compatibility. Sales reps can only delete their own tasks.

Get paginated notifications for the current user. Only returns notifications for subcategories where the bell channel is enabled in user preferences. System category notifications are excluded for non-administrators.

Response includes: notifications array, total count, page, per_page, and total_pages.

Lightweight endpoint for getting the unread notification count. Designed for heartbeat polling (15-60s intervals). Only counts notifications for subcategories where bell is enabled. Uses cached count for performance.

Response: { "unread_count": 5 }

Mark a single notification as read by providing its ID. Returns 404 if notification not found or doesn't belong to current user.

Response: { "success": true, "message": "Notification marked as read." }

Mark all unread notifications as read for the current user. Omit the 'id' parameter (or send empty body) to mark all.

Response: { "success": true, "message": "5 notifications marked as read.", "count": 5 }

Delete a specific notification by ID. Only the notification owner can delete it. Returns 404 if not found.

Response: { "success": true, "message": "Notification deleted." }

Update the current user's notification preferences. Both 'channels' and 'subcategories' are required.

Channels control global on/off for each delivery method (bell, email, browser).
Subcategories control per-notification-type channel settings.

Returns the updated preferences after save.

Get the default notification preferences structure before any user customization. Useful for resetting preferences or understanding the baseline configuration.

Returns same structure as Get Preferences but with factory defaults.

Get all available notification categories with metadata. Categories are filtered based on user capabilities:
- System: requires manage_options (administrators only)
- Campaigns, Automations, Forms, Integrations: require doublescale_manage
- Contacts, Pipeline, Tasks, Email Tracking: all CRM users

Each category includes: label, description, has_subcategories, subcategories_count.

Get subcategories for a specific notification category. The category path parameter is validated against known categories.

Valid categories: campaigns, automations, contacts, pipeline, tasks, email_tracking, forms, integrations, system.

Example: /subcategories/campaigns returns: email_campaigns, sms_campaigns, email_campaign_scheduled with labels and descriptions.
